details: Escalating conflict in the Gulf region has led to Brent crude oil prices climbing above $90 a barrel, following a ninth consecutive day of US military strikes against Iran. This geopolitical tension is exacerbating inflation fears, causing bonds to fall and stock markets to remain unsettled. Futures markets are now indicating an increased likelihood of at least one Federal Reserve interest rate hike by year-end, a move that typically impacts risk-sensitive assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Global Markets Brace as Oil Climbs Amid Gulf Conflict, Inflation Fears Mount

details: The cryptocurrency market faces a significant week driven by both US regulatory developments and a key European Central Bank (ECB) decision. In the US, a House Financial Services subcommittee will hold a hearing on FinCEN oversight on July 21. Upcoming deadlines include the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's (OCC) public comment period for GENIUS Act stablecoin regulations on July 24, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's (CFTC) comment period closure for a proposal on 24/7 Bitcoin perpetual futures trading on July 27. The ECB is widely anticipated to hold its benchmark interest rate steady on July 23.
title: US Regulatory Landscape and ECB Rate Decision Shape Week Ahead for Crypto

details: Despite a slight 2% recovery over the past week, Bitcoin is showing multiple bearish on-chain signals. Analysts point to approximately $2.3 billion in stablecoin outflows from major exchanges like Binance and Bybit over the last 30 days, suggesting a weakening of liquidity and softer buying demand. Furthermore, the Coinbase Premium Index has consistently remained negative since early May, indicating subdued institutional buying interest from US investors. These factors, combined with ongoing Middle East tensions, are contributing to a cautious sentiment in the crypto market.
title: Bitcoin Faces Bearish Signals Amid Macro Headwinds

details: The crypto market is anticipating a volatile week ahead due to a series of significant global macroeconomic events. These include China's interest rate decision (July 20), Japan's trade balance data, the European Central Bank's interest rate decision (July 23), upcoming US jobless claims and flash Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data, and major tech earnings reports from companies like Tesla, Alphabet, and Intel. While Bitcoin has demonstrated resilience, holding above $64,000 and supported by $264 million in net inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs, the confluence of these events is likely to introduce considerable market fluctuation.
title: Global Macro Calendar Expected to Drive Crypto Volatility
